characters.name: Bernard
characters.personality: precise, a little talkative, proud of his old silk-weavers' building

characters.name: Sylvie
characters.personality: quick, friendly, has seen every kind of parcel

characters.name: Inès
characters.personality: patient, apologetic, keen to fix things

characters.name: Dr Moreau
characters.personality: calm, thorough, explains things simply

characters.name: Romain
characters.personality: energetic, encouraging, says tu to everyone from the first minute

characters.name: Claire
characters.personality: calm, apologetic, efficient

titles.en: Visiting a flat in the Croix-Rousse

sceneNotes.en: A bright flat on the third floor of an old silk-weavers' building in the Croix-Rousse, with no lift; Bernard, the owner, shows you round.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Entrez, je vous en prie. Voilà le salon.

forms.text: Entrez, je vous en prie. Voilà le salon.

en.meaning: Come in, please. Here's the living room.
en.note: Je vous en prie = please, go ahead (it also means 'you're welcome'). French counts floors from le rez-de-chaussée, so le troisième étage is the US fourth floor.
en.literal: enter, I you of-it pray. there-is the living-room

expressions.pronunciationNote: Je vous en prie: zhuh voo-zahn PREE. Salon: sah-LON.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Il est vraiment lumineux, ce salon !

forms.text: Il est vraiment lumineux, ce salon !

en.meaning: This living room is really bright!
en.note: Lumineux (full of light) is the word every flat advert uses. The old canut flats of the Croix-Rousse are known for high ceilings and tall windows.
en.literal: it is really luminous, this living-room

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Et le loyer, c’est combien par mois ?

forms.text: Et le loyer, c’est combien par mois ?

en.meaning: And how much is the rent a month?
en.note: Le loyer = the rent. Naming the topic first, then asking c’est combien ?, is the natural spoken order.
en.literal: and the rent, it is how-much by month

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Huit cents euros, charges comprises.

forms.text: Huit cents euros, charges comprises.

en.meaning: Eight hundred euros, including service charges.
en.note: Charges comprises = service charges included (building upkeep, often water and heating); charges en plus = on top of the rent.
en.literal: eight hundreds euros, charges included

expressions.pronunciationNote: Huit cents euros: wee sahn-zuh-ROH. Comprises: kon-PREEZ.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Où est la machine à laver ?

forms.text: Où est la machine à laver ?

en.meaning: Where's the washing machine?
en.note: Une machine à laver (a machine to wash). À + infinitive says what a thing is for: une salle à manger, a dining room.
en.literal: where is the machine to wash

expressions.pronunciationNote: Machine à laver: mah-SHEEN ah lah-VAY.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Et le métro, c’est loin ?

forms.text: Et le métro, c’est loin ?

en.meaning: And is the metro far?
en.note: Answers you may hear: c’est tout près (it's very close), c’est à deux pas (it's two steps away).
en.literal: and the metro, it is far

expressions.pronunciationNote: Loin: lwan, nasal, no n sound.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: La machine est dans la cuisine, et le métro à cinq minutes.

forms.text: La machine est dans la cuisine, et le métro à cinq minutes.

en.meaning: The machine's in the kitchen, and the metro's five minutes away.
en.note: French drops a repeated verb just as English can: le métro (est) à cinq minutes. À + time = away: c’est à dix minutes à pied.
en.literal: the machine is in the kitchen, and the metro at five minutes

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Il est libre à partir de quand ?

forms.text: Il est libre à partir de quand ?

en.meaning: When is it available from?
en.note: Libre = free, available, for a flat, a table or a person. À partir de = from, starting from.
en.literal: it is free at to-leave from when

expressions.pronunciationNote: Libre: leebr. À partir de: ah par-TEER duh.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Dès le premier du mois. Mais attention, le voisin joue du piano !

forms.text: Dès le premier du mois. Mais attention, le voisin joue du piano !

en.meaning: From the first of the month. But be warned, the neighbour plays the piano!
en.note: Dès = from, as early as. Jouer du + instrument: jouer du piano, de la guitare; but jouer au + sport: jouer au foot.
en.literal: from the first of-the month. but attention, the neighbour plays some piano

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Pas de problème, j’aime la musique. Je le prends !

forms.text: Pas de problème, j’aime la musique. Je le prends !

en.meaning: No problem, I like music. I'll take it!
en.note: Le stands for l’appartement. Next step: you sign le bail, the lease, and make l’état des lieux, the check-in inventory.
en.literal: not of problem, I love the music. I it take

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Le dépôt de garantie, c’est combien ?

forms.text: Le dépôt de garantie, c’est combien ?

en.meaning: How much is the deposit?
en.note: Le dépôt de garantie, often called la caution, is the security deposit: by law at most one month's rent for an unfurnished flat.
en.literal: the deposit of guarantee, it is how-much

sceneNotes.en: The post office on a busy Saturday morning; you are sending a small box of presents to your family in Toronto, and the clerk offers a faster option.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Bonjour, je voudrais envoyer ce colis.

forms.text: Bonjour, je voudrais envoyer ce colis.

en.meaning: Hello, I'd like to send this parcel.
en.note: Je voudrais + infinitive = I'd like to. Un colis = a parcel; une lettre = a letter. La Poste also sells ready-made boxes.
en.literal: good-day, I would-like to-send this parcel

expressions.pronunciationNote: Envoyer: ahn-vwah-YAY. Colis: koh-LEE, silent s.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Très bien. C’est pour quel pays ?

forms.text: Très bien. C’est pour quel pays ?

en.meaning: Fine. Which country is it going to?
en.note: Quel agrees with its noun: quel pays, quelle ville, quels jours.
en.literal: very well. it is for which country

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Pour le Canada, à Toronto.

forms.text: Pour le Canada, à Toronto.

en.meaning: To Canada, to Toronto.
en.note: Countries take an article: le Canada, la France, les États-Unis. Going there: au Canada, en France, aux États-Unis; but à before a city: à Toronto.
en.literal: for the Canada, at Toronto

expressions.pronunciationNote: Canada: kah-nah-DAH, stressed at the end.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Posez-le sur la balance, s’il vous plaît.

forms.text: Posez-le sur la balance, s’il vous plaît.

en.meaning: Put it on the scales, please.
en.note: In a command, le comes after the verb with a hyphen: posez-le. Une balance = a pair of scales.
en.literal: put-it on the scales, if it you pleases

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Deux kilos, ça fait combien ?

forms.text: Deux kilos, ça fait combien ?

en.meaning: How much is it for two kilos?
en.note: Ça fait combien ? = how much does that come to? France weighs in kilos and grams: un kilo, cinq cents grammes.
en.literal: two kilos, that makes how-much

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Quarante-deux euros, ou soixante-cinq en express.

forms.text: Quarante-deux euros, ou soixante-cinq en express.

en.meaning: Forty-two euros, or sixty-five by express.
en.note: Soixante (60) is the last regular ten: seventy is soixante-dix, 'sixty-ten'. Express costs more but arrives sooner.
en.literal: forty-two euros, or sixty-five in express

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Et ça met combien de temps ?

forms.text: Et ça met combien de temps ?

en.meaning: And how long does it take?
en.note: Mettre du temps (to put time) = to take time: ça met une semaine. Combien de + noun = how much, how many.
en.literal: and that puts how-much of time

expressions.pronunciationNote: Met: meh. Temps: tahn, silent p and s.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Une semaine environ, ou trois jours en express.

forms.text: Une semaine environ, ou trois jours en express.

en.meaning: About a week, or three days by express.
en.note: Environ (about) can come before or after the amount: environ une semaine, une semaine environ.
en.literal: a week about, or three days in express

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Le moins cher, s’il vous plaît. Ce n’est pas urgent.

forms.text: Le moins cher, s’il vous plaît. Ce n’est pas urgent.

en.meaning: The cheaper one, please. It's not urgent.
en.note: Le moins cher = the least expensive; le plus rapide = the fastest.
en.literal: the less expensive, if it you pleases. it not is not urgent

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Je vous règle par carte.

forms.text: Je vous règle par carte.

en.meaning: I'll pay you by card.
en.note: Régler (to settle) is a polite verb for paying at a counter: je vous règle par carte, en espèces. Payer works too.
en.literal: I you settle by card

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: C’est pour envoyer un colis au Canada.

forms.text: C’est pour envoyer un colis au Canada.

en.meaning: I'm here to send a parcel to Canada.
en.note: C’est pour + infinitive = I'm here to: the usual way to state your business at a counter. To collect a parcel: c’est pour retirer un colis.
en.literal: it is for to-send a parcel to-the Canada

sceneNotes.en: The customer service desk of a home appliance shop on the rue de la République; the kettle you bought there last week doesn't heat.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Bonjour, qu’est-ce que je peux faire pour vous ?

forms.text: Bonjour, qu’est-ce que je peux faire pour vous ?

en.meaning: Hello, what can I do for you?
en.note: The standard opening at a service desk. Answer with bonjour first: in a French shop, the greeting always comes before the problem.
en.literal: good-day, what is-it that I can to-do for you

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Bonjour, cette bouilloire ne chauffe pas.

forms.text: Bonjour, cette bouilloire ne chauffe pas.

en.meaning: Hello, this kettle doesn't heat up.
en.note: Une bouilloire = a kettle (from bouillir, to boil). Chauffer = to heat. For anything that doesn't work at all: ça ne marche pas.
en.literal: good-day, this kettle not heats not

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Je l’ai achetée ici la semaine dernière.

forms.text: Je l’ai achetée ici la semaine dernière.

en.meaning: I bought it here last week.
en.note: With l’ (the kettle, feminine) placed before avoir, the participle takes an e in writing: je l’ai achetée. It sounds just like acheté.
en.literal: I it-have bought here the week last

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Je suis désolée. Vous avez le ticket de caisse ?

forms.text: Je suis désolée. Vous avez le ticket de caisse ?

en.meaning: I'm sorry. Do you have the receipt?
en.note: Le ticket de caisse = the till receipt; un reçu is more formal. Shops usually ask for it before any refund or exchange.
en.literal: I am sorry. you have the ticket of till

expressions.pronunciationNote: Ticket de caisse: tee-KAY duh KESS.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Ce n’est pas grave. Oui, le voici.

forms.text: Ce n’est pas grave. Oui, le voici.

en.meaning: That's all right. Yes, here it is.
en.note: Ce n’est pas grave (it's not serious) = no problem, that's all right. Le voici = here it is; la voici for a feminine noun.
en.literal: it not is not serious. yes, it here-is

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Merci. Je vous la rembourse ?

forms.text: Merci. Je vous la rembourse ?

en.meaning: Thank you. Shall I refund it?
en.note: Rembourser = to refund. A present-tense statement with a rising voice works as an offer: je vous la rembourse ? = shall I refund it for you?
en.literal: thanks. I to-you it refund

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Vous pouvez plutôt me l’échanger ?

forms.text: Vous pouvez plutôt me l’échanger ?

en.meaning: Could you exchange it for me instead?
en.note: Plutôt = instead, rather. Two pronouns go in this order: me l’échanger = exchange it for me.
en.literal: you can rather to-me it-exchange

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Bien sûr. Tenez, celle-ci est neuve.

forms.text: Bien sûr. Tenez, celle-ci est neuve.

en.meaning: Of course. Here you are, this one is brand new.
en.note: Tenez = here you are, as you hand something over. Neuf, neuve = brand new; nouveau, nouvelle = new, another one.
en.literal: well sure. hold, this-one-here is new

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Merci, vous êtes très aimable.

forms.text: Merci, vous êtes très aimable.

en.meaning: Thank you, that's very kind of you.
en.note: Vous êtes très aimable is a warm, polite thank-you for good service.
en.literal: thanks, you are very kind

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Elle ne marche pas du tout.

forms.text: Elle ne marche pas du tout.

en.meaning: It doesn't work at all.
en.note: Marcher (to walk) also means 'to work' for machines: ça marche ! = it works! Pas du tout = not at all. Elle because une bouilloire is feminine.
en.literal: she not walks not at-all

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Je peux en avoir une autre ?

forms.text: Je peux en avoir une autre ?

en.meaning: Can I have another one?
en.note: En = of them: je peux en avoir une autre ? = can I have another (of them)? Say un autre for a masculine noun.
en.literal: I can of-them to-have an other

sceneNotes.en: A GP's surgery in your neighbourhood; you have had a sore throat and a slight fever for two days, and Dr Moreau has a slot at 5 p.m.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Bonjour, docteur.

forms.text: Bonjour, docteur.

en.meaning: Good afternoon, doctor.
en.note: Docteur is how you address a doctor; when you talk about one, say un médecin. From about 6 p.m., say bonsoir instead.
en.literal: good-day, doctor

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Bonjour, asseyez-vous. Qu’est-ce qui vous amène ?

forms.text: Bonjour, asseyez-vous. Qu’est-ce qui vous amène ?

en.meaning: Hello, have a seat. What brings you here?
en.note: Qu’est-ce qui vous amène ? (what brings you?) is the doctor's usual first question. Asseyez-vous = sit down.
en.literal: good-day, sit-yourself. what is-it that you brings

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: J’ai mal à la gorge, et un peu de fièvre.

forms.text: J’ai mal à la gorge, et un peu de fièvre.

en.meaning: I have a sore throat and a slight fever.
en.note: Avoir mal à + body part: mal à la gorge (throat), mal à la tête (head), mal au ventre (stomach). Fever is measured in Celsius: 38 °C counts as fever.
en.literal: I have bad at the throat, and a little of fever

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Depuis combien de temps ?

forms.text: Depuis combien de temps ?

en.meaning: For how long?
en.note: Depuis = since, for. French uses the present with depuis where English needs 'have had': j’ai mal depuis deux jours.
en.literal: since how-much of time

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Depuis deux jours, à peu près.

forms.text: Depuis deux jours, à peu près.

en.meaning: For about two days.
en.note: À peu près = about, roughly. You can also give a starting point: depuis samedi, depuis hier soir.
en.literal: since two days, at little near

expressions.pronunciationNote: À peu près: ah puh PREH.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: C’est une petite angine. Je vous prescris un sirop.

forms.text: C’est une petite angine. Je vous prescris un sirop.

en.meaning: It's a mild throat infection. I'm prescribing you a syrup.
en.note: False friend: une angine is a throat infection, not angina. Take the prescription, l’ordonnance, to any pharmacy.
en.literal: it is a little throat-infection. I you prescribe a syrup

expressions.pronunciationNote: Angine: ahn-ZHEEN. Sirop: see-ROH, silent p.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Je le prends combien de fois par jour ?

forms.text: Je le prends combien de fois par jour ?

en.meaning: How many times a day do I take it?
en.note: Combien de fois = how many times. Une fois, deux fois counts occasions; une heure is the time on the clock.
en.literal: I it take how-much of times by day

expressions.pronunciationNote: Fois: fwah. Par jour: par ZHOOR.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Trois fois par jour, après les repas. C’est clair pour vous ?

forms.text: Trois fois par jour, après les repas. C’est clair pour vous ?

en.meaning: Three times a day, after meals. Is that clear for you?
en.note: C’est clair pour vous ? = is that clear? Doctors and pharmacists check that you have understood a dosage; don't be shy to ask again.
en.literal: three times by day, after the meals. it is clear for you

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Oui, c’est clair. Trois fois par jour.

forms.text: Oui, c’est clair. Trois fois par jour.

en.meaning: Yes, that's clear. Three times a day.
en.note: Repeating the key information back is the best way to show, and to check, that you have understood.
en.literal: yes, it is clear. three times by day

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Merci beaucoup, docteur. Au revoir !

forms.text: Merci beaucoup, docteur. Au revoir !

en.meaning: Thank you very much, doctor. Goodbye!
en.note: A GP visit costs 30 euros; with a carte Vitale, the French health card, most of it is paid back by the Sécurité sociale.
en.literal: thanks much, doctor. to-the seeing-again

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: J’ai très mal quand j’avale.

forms.text: J’ai très mal quand j’avale.

en.meaning: It really hurts when I swallow.
en.note: Avaler = to swallow. Quand + present = when: j’ai mal quand je parle, quand je mange.
en.literal: I have very bad when I swallow

sceneNotes.en: A running club that meets on the banks of the Rhône; Romain, the coach, says tu to everyone, and the first month is free.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Bonjour ! Les entraînements, c’est quels jours ?

forms.text: Bonjour ! Les entraînements, c’est quels jours ?

en.meaning: Hello! Which days are the training sessions?
en.note: Un entraînement = a training session. Quels jours ? = which days? Topic first, then the question: very common in spoken French.
en.literal: good-day! the trainings, it is which days

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Le mardi et le jeudi, à dix-neuf heures.

forms.text: Le mardi et le jeudi, à dix-neuf heures.

en.meaning: Tuesdays and Thursdays, at 7 p.m.
en.note: Le mardi = on Tuesdays, every week. Dix-neuf heures = 7 p.m.: clubs and timetables use the 24-hour clock.
en.literal: the Tuesday and the Thursday, at nineteen hours

expressions.pronunciationNote: Dix-neuf heures: deez-nuh-VUHR; the f of neuf sounds like v before heures.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Et l’inscription, c’est combien ?

forms.text: Et l’inscription, c’est combien ?

en.meaning: And how much is it to join?
en.note: L’inscription = signing up, and the fee for it. Most French clubs charge a yearly fee, la cotisation, often paid in September.
en.literal: and the inscription, it is how-much

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Le premier mois est gratuit, puis c’est cent euros par an.

forms.text: Le premier mois est gratuit, puis c’est cent euros par an.

en.meaning: The first month is free, then it's a hundred euros a year.
en.note: Gratuit = free of charge; libre = free as in available. Cent links to euros with a t sound.
en.literal: the first month is free, then it is hundred euros by year

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Je peux venir faire un essai jeudi ?

forms.text: Je peux venir faire un essai jeudi ?

en.meaning: Can I come and try it out on Thursday?
en.note: Faire un essai = to have a trial session. Jeudi without le = this Thursday.
en.literal: I can to-come to-do a try Thursday

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Bien sûr ! Tu cours combien de kilomètres, en général ?

forms.text: Bien sûr ! Tu cours combien de kilomètres, en général ?

en.meaning: Of course! How many kilometres do you usually run?
en.note: In sports clubs everyone says tu, the coach included. Courir: je cours, tu cours, il court; the final letters are silent.
en.literal: well sure! you run how-many of kilometres, in general

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Environ cinq. J’adore courir au bord de l’eau !

forms.text: Environ cinq. J’adore courir au bord de l’eau !

en.meaning: About five. I love running by the water!
en.note: Au bord de = at the edge of, by: au bord de l’eau, au bord de la mer. Cinq stands alone: kilomètres is understood.
en.literal: about five. I adore to-run at-the edge of the water

expressions.pronunciationNote: Courir: koo-REER. Au bord de l’eau: oh BOR duh LOH.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Super ! Rendez-vous jeudi au pont de la Guillotière.

forms.text: Super ! Rendez-vous jeudi au pont de la Guillotière.

en.meaning: Great! See you Thursday at the Guillotière bridge.
en.note: Rendez-vous ! = let's meet; un rendez-vous is also an appointment. The Pont de la Guillotière is one of the bridges over the Rhône.
en.literal: super! meeting Thursday at-the bridge of the Guillotière

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Parfait, à jeudi, dix-neuf heures !

forms.text: Parfait, à jeudi, dix-neuf heures !

en.meaning: Perfect, see you Thursday at seven!
en.note: À + day = see you then: à jeudi, à lundi. Repeating the time is a simple way to confirm a plan.
en.literal: perfect, to Thursday, nineteen hours

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Est-ce que je peux juste regarder, la première fois ?

forms.text: Est-ce que je peux juste regarder, la première fois ?

en.meaning: Can I just watch the first time?
en.note: Est-ce que je peux… ? is a little more careful than je peux… ?. Juste = just, only, in everyday speech.
en.literal: is-it that I can just to-watch, the first time

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Courir, ça me fait du bien.

forms.text: Courir, ça me fait du bien.

en.meaning: Running does me good.
en.note: Ça me fait du bien = it does me good. Naming the activity first, then picking it up with ça, is typical of spoken French.
en.literal: to-run, that to-me does some good

sceneNotes.en: The baggage desk at Lyon Saint-Exupéry airport; your flight from London landed an hour ago, but your big blue suitcase never came out.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Excusez-moi, c’est ici pour les bagages perdus ?

forms.text: Excusez-moi, c’est ici pour les bagages perdus ?

en.meaning: Excuse me, is this the place for lost luggage?
en.note: Les bagages is plural in French where English says 'luggage': mes bagages = my luggage, un bagage = one bag.
en.literal: excuse-me, it is here for the luggages lost

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Oui, c’est bien ici. Que se passe-t-il ?

forms.text: Oui, c’est bien ici. Que se passe-t-il ?

en.meaning: Yes, this is the right place. What's the problem?
en.note: Que se passe-t-il ? is the formal form of qu’est-ce qui se passe ?: verb and subject swap, and -t- is added between two vowels.
en.literal: yes, it is well here. what itself passes-t-it

expressions.pronunciationNote: Que se passe-t-il: kuh suh pahss-TEEL.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Ma valise n’est pas arrivée.

forms.text: Ma valise n’est pas arrivée.

en.meaning: My suitcase didn't arrive.
en.note: Arriver takes être in the passé composé, so the participle agrees with the subject: ma valise n’est pas arrivée. It sounds the same as arrivé.
en.literal: my suitcase not is not arrived

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Je suis arrivé de Londres il y a une heure.

forms.text: Je suis arrivé de Londres il y a une heure.

en.meaning: I arrived from London an hour ago.
en.note: Il y a + time = ago: il y a une heure, il y a deux jours. A woman writes arrivée; it sounds the same.
en.literal: I am arrived from London there-has an hour

expressions.pronunciationNote: Londres: LONDR. Il y a une heure: eel-yah ün UHR.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Je suis désolée, elle est restée à Londres.

forms.text: Je suis désolée, elle est restée à Londres.

en.meaning: I'm sorry, it stayed behind in London.
en.note: False friend: rester means to stay, to remain, not 'to rest'. Elle est restée: rester takes être too.
en.literal: I am sorry, she is stayed at London

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Quand est-ce que je vais la récupérer ?

forms.text: Quand est-ce que je vais la récupérer ?

en.meaning: When will I get it back?
en.note: Récupérer = to get back, to collect. La stands for la valise and goes before the infinitive: je vais la récupérer.
en.literal: when is-it that I go it to-recover

expressions.pronunciationNote: Quand est-ce que: kahn-TESS-kuh; the d sounds like t. Récupérer: ray-kü-pay-RAY.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: Demain matin. On vous la livre à quelle adresse ?

forms.text: Demain matin. On vous la livre à quelle adresse ?

en.meaning: Tomorrow morning. Which address shall we deliver it to?
en.note: Livrer = to deliver. Spelling trap: adresse has one d and two s in French, the reverse of English 'address'.
en.literal: tomorrow morning. one to-you it delivers at which address

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Chez moi, s’il vous plaît : 12, rue Burdeau.

forms.text: Chez moi, s’il vous plaît : 12, rue Burdeau.

en.meaning: To my home, please: 12 rue Burdeau.
en.note: Chez moi = at my place, to my home. A French address starts with the number, then the street: 12, rue Burdeau, 69001 Lyon.
en.literal: at-home-of me, if it you pleases: 12, street Burdeau

expressions.pronunciationNote: Chez moi: shay MWAH. Douze: dooz.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: C’est noté. Voici votre numéro de dossier.

forms.text: C’est noté. Voici votre numéro de dossier.

en.meaning: That's noted. Here's your file number.
en.note: C’est noté = noted, that's done. Keep le numéro de dossier (the file reference) to track your suitcase online.
en.literal: it is noted. here-is your number of file

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Merci beaucoup, madame. Bonne soirée !

forms.text: Merci beaucoup, madame. Bonne soirée !

en.meaning: Thank you very much. Have a good evening!
en.note: Bonne soirée = have a nice evening; bonne journée during the day. Adding madame or monsieur makes a thank-you warmer.
en.literal: thanks much, madam. good evening

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: Mon sac à dos n’est pas sur le tapis.

forms.text: Mon sac à dos n’est pas sur le tapis.

en.meaning: My backpack isn't on the carousel.
en.note: Le tapis (à bagages) = the baggage carousel; un tapis is also a rug. Un sac à dos (a bag on the back) = a backpack.
en.literal: my bag at back not is not on the carpet

expressions.pronunciationNote: Sac à dos: sah-kah-DOH. Tapis: tah-PEE.
